title: Five Indian-Origin Men Face Extortion, Weapons and Drug Charges in BC Task-Force Sweep
excerpt: Langley RCMP's 16-month Project E_PURSUANCE ended with arrests, firearms and drug seizures — and more charges are expected across BC and Alberta.
body:
• Five men of Indian origin — Sanket Singla (23), Sahil (24), Simranjeet Singh (24), Harsh (21) and Jagdeep Singh (24) — face charges of extortion, reckless discharge of firearms, arson and drug trafficking after the 16-month investigation Project E_PURSUANCE, with bail hearings set for October 5 in Surrey.
  • The case began in June 2025 when co-owners of an auto dealership in Langley reported significant extortion demands, followed by two targeted attacks — arson and shootings — at the business's Surrey and Langley locations last summer.
  • Sanket Singla was arrested on arrival at Toronto Pearson International Airport after a controlled operation involving immigration and RCMP liaison officers facilitated his entry from India; the other four were arrested in Surrey.
  • Police seized four firearms, ammunition and magazines, plus suspected fentanyl, cocaine and opium; investigators say evidence points to additional suspects in BC and Alberta, with more charges expected.

The Charge Sheet

The BC Prosecution Service laid the charges on October 1. Sanket Singla faces extortion, two counts of recklessly discharging a firearm into or at a place, two counts of causing damage by fire or explosion, and throwing an explosive substance with intent to destroy property — CBC reported Molotov cocktails thrown into the auto shop.

Sahil of Surrey faces extortion, arson, three counts of unauthorized transfer of prohibited firearms, three counts of unauthorized transfer of prohibited devices or ammunition, and two counts of trafficking cocaine. Simranjeet Singh, Harsh and Jagdeep Singh face combinations of extortion, reckless firearm discharge, arson and explosives charges. All five remain in custody ahead of their October 5 bail hearings in Surrey.

A Task-Force Operation

The investigation was run by Langley RCMP in a joint operation with the Combined Forces Special Enforcement Unit of BC and the Federal Policing Pacific Region through the province's Provincial Extortion Task Force, with international RCMP liaison officers, the Canada Border Services Agency and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada also involved.

"I want to sincerely thank the victims for their courage in coming forward, their support throughout the investigation, and the trust they placed in us to thoroughly investigate this matter and bring it before the courts."

— Supt. Harm Dosange, Officer in Charge, Langley RCMP

At the October 2 press conference, Dosange was blunt about the strategy: "The RCMP's position was we were going to target the higher levels of the extortion and hold them accountable." He added: "Numerous times we sat with the victims, and we heard the same message: 'We came here. Our life's work. We've worked hard. Now people are trying to take that away from us.'"

"These files are complex and resource intensive, and they often require specialized police resources in different roles to advance them."

— Chief Supt. Duncan Pound, Lower Mainland District, RCMP

More to Come

Investigators say evidence points to possible additional suspects in extortions and violence across British Columbia and Alberta, and more charges are expected. The case is part of a broader pattern the province's extortion task force is pursuing — a series of cases largely targeting South Asian business owners and community members since the task force was launched in 2025. Reports in some outlets of links to gangster Lawrence Bishnoi remain unconfirmed; the official RCMP release makes no such claim.

Diaspora Angle

The extortion wave gripping BC's South Asian business community — immigrant entrepreneurs who, as Dosange put it, came here with their "life's work" and now face armed intimidation — has become one of the top diaspora safety issues in Canada. These arrests are the biggest scalp yet for the province's anti-extortion task force, and the case only proceeded because the victims came forward.
